findings.title: The glossary defines the highest root by a rule that also gives the highest short root on 16 of the 32 boards of finite type
findings.claim: The new definition reads 'On a board of finite type, the root population at which no mutation raises any city.' On B_n, C_n, F4 and G2 two root populations satisfy this: the highest root and the highest short root. A reader who applies the rule as written can call the highest short root 'the highest root'.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.7 and 4 T9 distinguish the highest root from the highest short root (T9: 'the highest root, or the highest short root after a start at a short city'). The rule is unique only on simply laced boards, which is the context of M1 beat 3, where the sentence was first used for E8.
findings.observed: Oracle (lie_games.mutate on cartan(letter,n) over roots): B3 gives [(1,2,2), (1,1,1)]; C3 gives [(1,2,1), (2,2,1)]; F4 gives [(2,3,4,2), (1,2,3,2)]; G2 gives [(2,1), (3,2)]. In all, 16 of 32 boards have two such roots. On /atlas/B3/ the highest root is (1,2,2) and (1,1,1) is named the highest short root.
findings.reproduction: npm ci; npm run build; python3 redteam/redteam-RT-13-p6-oracle-highest.py reference site/dist (it prints the glossary's definition and the roots per board; exits 1)
findings.specRef: SPEC 2.7; 4 T9 ('the highest root, or the highest short root after a start at a short city'); 8.4 'Define every term'; RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 ('a mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong')
findings.proposedFix: Restrict the definition to boards with single roads, or say 'the root population of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city', as the Atlas pages do. Add 'highest short root' to the entry.
